card: Refactors kernel fatal and flush error notifications to use typed representations instead of translated bilingual_str objects. Defines kernel::FlushError as an enum and kernel::FatalError as a variant holding context types, moving user-facing string construction and translation out of the kernel into node::KernelNotifications. Also updates the kernel C API callbacks to expose error codes rather than strings. This is a step toward removing translation.h from libbitcoinkernel as tracked in #27587.
evidence: Part of the Bitcoin Kernel Library tracking issue #27587, specifically addressing the item 'Remove translation.h usage from the kernel' (PR description).
problem: kernel::Notifications::fatalError() and flushError() accepted bilingual_str arguments, unnecessarily pulling application-level translation dependencies (util/translation.h) and UI-facing string logic into libbitcoinkernel.

risk.why: A mistake in error mapping or notification dispatch could prevent a clean node shutdown during disk failure or block validation errors.

scope_notes: Adds src/kernel/error.h and changes the signature of C API callbacks btck_NotifyFlushError and btck_NotifyFatalError to drop the formatted message string in favor of error codes.
summary: Replace string-based fatal and flush error notifications in the kernel interface with typed structures. Defines kernel::FlushError as an enum and kernel::FatalError as a std::variant of error-specific context structs, moving string generation and translation into the node layer. Also modifies the kernel C API error callbacks to emit numeric error codes instead of formatted text.
